A Villain By Any Other Name...

Silvia_Goddess_of_Being_Right

Summary:

In the wake of Leviathan, the remaining Wards have to contend with a potential new member.

Notes:

Huge thanks to HQM and Derived for looking this over. They gave invaluable critique and without it this fic would have so many terrible sentences.

Chapter 1: Clockblocker

Notes:

(See the end of the chapter for notes.)

Chapter Text

Dennis is tired. Patrols in the ruins of Brockton Bay are exhausting, and he hasn't had time to process his grief. The Ward team is half the size it used to be, and the absence of his friends weighs on him. Part of him isn’t looking forward to having the time to actually think about that, once reinforcements arrive; replacements, if he wants to be realistic. Home is worse, given how stressful his dad's situation has become. Dennis needs to talk to Panacea about it, but she’s always so busy—and frankly, a bit off putting at the best of times.

At least the PRT building is active, and there’s plenty to keep his attention. All the staff and heroes relocated here from the Protectorate HQ after it was washed ashore by the Endbringer. With the state of the city, people—including himself—roam the halls even this late at night. Harried accountants, agents on their third consecutive shift, a blonde girl about his age scowling at a vending machine—Dennis stops, and stares. She's tall for a girl, with dirty blonde hair and a few freckles peaking out of her PRT issue domino mask. Her outfit is very obviously civilian clothing, consisting of an oversized hoodie for Brockton University, and a pair of worn jeans.

There aren’t many people of Ward age around the base. A few of the PRT staff brought their families here to shelter temporarily, but they’re few enough that Dennis already knows them all. She could be one of them, but then the non-capes don’t tend to wear masks. Looking closer, he spots a guest lanyard hanging from a belt buckle, so she’s definitely supposed to be here.

After a moment of contemplation, the girl hits a few buttons, and one of the bags of chips starts to fall... only to get caught part way down. Her scowl deepens. Dennis steps forward, propelled by curiosity and loneliness.

"Machine giving you trouble?" he asks with forced amusement. The girl jerks her head towards him, eyes narrowing in what he swears is hostility.

She scans her gaze across him, from the clocks on his costume to the flat pane of his full face-mask. For some reason, Dennis feels as if she can see right through it, and is staring into his soul. Unnerving, but probably just his nerves.

"Damn thing stole my dollar," she says after a moment. To punctuate her point, she smacks the glass. Nothing happens, aside from attracting the attention of a few passerbys.

"Yeah, these things are rough. Want some help?" Dennis makes to grab the machine, only to stop when she tenses. He puts down his hand, and he sees her relax again. Then, as if realizing what just happened, her face twitches with annoyance and her cheeks go just a shade pinker.

"Nah, it's fine." She turns back to the machine. "I can solve it better myself anyway. See, these machines all have maintenance codes on them, that way they can be refilled or repaired by any tech or janitor."

Dennis's eyes widen behind his mask as she puts in a combination of eight different numbers, and ends it with two pound signs. The door pops open, and she snags her bag of chips.

"Want anything while I have it open?" she asks with an arched eyebrow.

Dennis suddenly becomes aware of the cameras on the wall, powered by the tinkertech generators Dragon was kind enough to provide. "Nah, I'm good."

The girl just shrugs. "Suit yourself."

Contrary to his expectations, she doesn't take anything else. Just shuts the door, and starts walking down the hall towards the elevator. Dennis falls into step next to her, thanking his luck that she's going in the direction he'd been going originally. It would be way too awkward to go back the way he came just to follow her.

"That's a neat trick you've got there," he comments neutrally. She doesn't respond, outside of a glance to confirm that she knows he's there. "Haven't seen you around before. New in town?"

Are you a new Ward?

A small smile twitches at the side of her face. "Nah, you've definitely seen me around before."

They pull to a stop in front of the elevator. "I have?" Dennis asks dumbly.

"Totally." The girl opens the elevator, steps in, and stops before he can start to follow. "You're heading down the right hall, right?" He is, but he doesn't know how she knows that. Her smile widens. "See you around, Clock."

Dennis stares at the closed elevator doors, and spends some time trying to figure out what just happened.

Notes:

Wrote this fic after rereading some of arc 9. I've always thought that post leviathan could be a decent place to have Lisa join the Wards, but there's a lot of odd logistical issues with it. I think I've gotten around enough of them here, and tbh I'm pretty happy with how this turned out.
Clockblocker is a character I like now. I didn't use to like him, but after Curiosity and this, I've come to appreciate his character. It's really funny coming around on someone like that, lol.
(speaking of Curiosity, it's not dead. I've been extremely busy with work and stuck on a chapter. Luckily, I made a breakthrough when I decided to scrap the entire draft and write a different scene, so with any luck it'll come out soon™)

I have this entire story pre-written, and it's not actually that long. I'm just splitting it into five parts because I like having the PoVs separate, and I'll post one a day until this is complete.
So, stay tuned for the rest!

Chapter 2: Kid Win

Notes:

Another round of thanks to HQM and Derived, who pulled this chapter from the fetid fields of typo-despair.

(See the end of the chapter for more notes.)

Chapter Text

Armsmaster got kicked out of the Protectorate. Kid Win isn't completely sure why, but he suspects it has something to do with the armband failures. His own armband broke, and he hid it so he could take it apart and find out why. Fried by an EMP, as it turns out. Lots of people died because of that move, and still more are completely unaccounted for. It's uncomfortable to think about, so Chris largely hasn't.

One way or another, that means things are even more chaotic than usual. Dragon's around to help with repairs, but Chris finds himself getting involved more often than his parents would like. They want him out of the program entirely, but he's not sure that would help. He likes the Wards, mostly. They're his friends, and frankly being an independent Tinker sounds miserable. It’s bad enough being a Tinker with the backing of the government.

The door to the common room buzzes, and everyone jerks to attention. Clockblocker dozes in an armchair, Vista pretends to read a book, and Shadow Stalker broods against a nearby wall. Actually, Shadow Stalker might have been asleep as well, but Chris can never really tell with her. Glory Girl is also here, despite technically not being a Ward. Rumor has it that she's been considering joining up, or at the very least working more closely than before. Regardless, the whole team was told to be here for an important meeting. An announcement of some sort. The higher ups were cagey about the details, but then they usually are.

When the doors open, it's to admit Director Piggot and a girl around Chris's age. Maybe a bit older, actually, given her height. Blonde, with sharp green eyes that make Chris look away on instinct.

"Good afternoon, Wards, Glory Girl," Director Piggot says with a curt nod.

The team returns the greeting, all without looking away from the mysterious girl. She has her hands in the pockets of her massive hoodie, and seems to be sizing up each member of the team individually. For some reason, her eyes linger on Shadow Stalker longer than the others.

"I know everyone is tired, so I'll get straight to the point." Piggot locks eyes with Clockblocker's mask, and Chris is once again reminded of Aegis's absence. "This is Tattletale, and she'll be staying here until further notice."

The girl, Tattletale, smirks.

"What the h—" "So that's what you meant—" "Director, why—"

Director Piggot raises a hand, and everyone goes silent. Everyone, that is, except for Tattletale.

"Wow, you've got them whipped," she drawls.

Director Piggot shoots Tattletale a dirty look, and refocuses on the team. "To preemptively answer a few questions: yes, she was a member of the Undersiders. She's cooperating with us and is looking for a spot on the team. There are some complications, even outside the entire situation we're currently facing, and as such we'd like all of you to keep this to yourselves. Yes, Glory Girl?"

Glory Girl puts down her hand. "What about New Wave?"

"They'll be brought up to speed shortly," Director Piggot responds smoothly. "Your family is on their way here to be briefed. You are welcome to sit in, but it won't be anything more than you're learning right now."

As Director Piggot fields more questions, Chris stares at the blonde villain. She's still smirking, but hasn't interjected again. She seems almost lost. Passive, and quieter than he expected. Then again, he only knows her from a few confrontations, and parahuman combat is hardly the best way to get to know someone.

"Now if there's nothing else…" The director trails off, before nodding to herself. "Play nice, I don't want more paperwork."

She leaves, and all attention goes back to Tattletale.

"Why are you here?" Vista asks with a scowl.

"Weren’t you listening?" Tattletale tilts her head to the side. "I'm going straight. Trading my black hat for a white one, as it were."

"You really think it's that easy?" Glory Girl asks with a scowl. "After how you treated all of us?"

Tattletale doesn't even have the decency to look guilty. "I mean, why not? You're all fine."

"My sister can barely sleep after what you said to her," Glory Girl hisses.

"Your sister needed a reality check a year ago," Tattletale snaps back.

"Hey," Shadow Stalker speaks up. Tattletale looks at her. "What happened to that Grue guy?"

Tattletale's expression darkens. "Oh that's rich. Not even on your side for five minutes, and you already want me to rat out my old teammate so you can slit his throat."

Shadow Stalker snorts. "Wow, that's dramatic. Guess that means he bit it."

Tattletale's hands ball into fists, and Chris is struck by a sudden realization. "Oh. I get it." Tattletale whips around to look at him, a barb on her tongue. "Sorry for your loss," Chris finishes lamely.

Whatever she's about to say catches in her throat, and it looks like she swallowed a lemon. Then her expression smooths out and she turns back towards Shadow Stalker. "You're just lucky I'm the forgive-and-forget type, because someone less magnanimous than me wouldn't be willing to overlook how you've treated two of my teammates."

"Two of them?" Shadow Stalker balks. "Who's the other one?"

Before Tattletale can respond, Vista stands up and puts herself between the pair. She stares the villain dead in the eye as she speaks. "Why don't you go somewhere else? Somewhere with less enemies?"

Tattletale stares back, her smile somewhat fragile. "Wouldn't you like to know, shorty."

Vista tightens her fists… then relaxes. "Whatever. I'm going on patrol."

She marches stiffly out of the room, and Shadow Stalker moves to follow. "I'll go with. Need to go somewhere a bit more heroic."

If Tattletale is bothered, she doesn't show it. Instead, she locks eyes with Clockblocker and Glory Girl in turn. Chris ducks his head down, and keeps fiddling with the armband. Ultimately, this will pass. Tattletale may be annoying, but she has a point that none of their conflicts were really that big of a deal. There's a lot to do, and plenty to keep busy. Things will work themselves out.

"So, Glory Girl, have you decided what name you’re going to pick when you rebrand? I think you could pull off Gory Girl, if you wanted to get a more mature image."

Things will probably work themselves out.

 

Notes:

Kid Win is an interesting cape. Moreso than most people give him credit for—including myself tbh. The way his ADHD interacts with his power is fascinating, and I've used him as a reference before when writing neurodivergent capes. He's also got a fun amount of insecurity and dork energy, while still managing to be somewhat smart.
I frequently call him "the most bulliable Ward (affectionate)", and really I should write him more for that reason alone.

It hasn't been 24 hours, but I did sleep and wake up so I figure this is fine. Especially since slay the spire 2 is releasing today I have work later so it's either post it early, or really late.

Chapter 3: Vista

Notes:

Derived and HQM beta read this as well, which I'm sure comes as a complete surprise at this point. What's not a surprise is the good work they put into beta reading it <3

(See the end of the chapter for more notes.)

Chapter Text

After Victoria slams the door behind her with a bang, Vista looks up from the book she’s pretending to read. Normally loud noises make her jump, but the constant patrols and fitful sleep have dulled her reactions to the point that she doesn’t even flinch.

"I've just about had it with her!" Victoria says, half floating and half pacing about the common room. She runs a hand through her hair, not quite pulling at it despite her frustration.

"Tattletale, or Shadow Stalker?" Vista asks. The latter has quickly become the lesser of two evils, even if she's been a bit more intense than usual. Something about the city has her on edge.

Not that the rest of them are any different.

"Tattletale," Victoria spits out the name like it's a curse. "She's just so. So. Ugh."

"Yeah." Vista doesn't have much to offer beyond hollow platitudes. She doesn't like Tattletale, but it's hard to care about that. Easier to focus on the day-to-day. Saving people, clearing streets, and just… all of that. It's a lot, but she can handle it.

She has to.

"She keeps needling me about my sister. Making these nonsensical statements, then mocking me when I ask for clarification. If I didn't know any better, I'd say she was trying to drive us apart." Victoria's fists tighten and loosen repeatedly.

"Is Amy doing okay?" Vista asks obligingly.

"She's…" Victoria slumps. "Distant. Something has her unsettled, off balance. I'm worried, and I don't know if I can do anything about it."

Vista looks away. Dean had mentioned something about Amy's problems, back before… before…

He wasn't specific, but he was trying to help. Of course he was, the sweet dolt. Vista could imagine how crushing it would be to have someone trying to help, someone who cared, only to have them ripped away. Not to mention the weight of being a healer in the aftermath of an Endbringer.

"There's a lot going on," Vista says, rather than vocalizing any of her thoughts. "Maybe she just needs to process."

Victoria sits down in a chair, and stares at the ground. "Yeah, maybe."

There's a long silence.

"I miss him, you know," Victoria says quietly.

Vista's throat tightens. "Me too."

The silence stretches even longer, until the door to the common room opens. Tattletale strolls in and seems to visibly perk up when she sees Victoria. "Hey, Victory Lass, any luck on the new name?"

"You're not even trying with that one," Victoria snaps.

Vista watches as the pair trades barbs back and forth. As Victoria slowly livens up and the grief seeps into the background. If Vista didn’t know any better, she’d think that the villain was doing this for Victoria’s benefit. Tattletale meets Vista's gaze, grins, and winks.

She's doing this on purpose, Vista realizes. Maybe Tattletale's not that bad after all.

"Look at it this way G-Lady, at least you're old enough to actually make these decisions," Tattletale looks at Vista with some exaggeration. "Some people still need their hands held when signing documents."

Nevermind, she's the worst, Vista thinks as she joins the argument.

 

Notes:

Vista is tricky for me because I do genuinely dislike her as a character. By Ward, I like her a bit more, but not to the point of wanting to write about her. She's not a bad character, nor one I find completely uninteresting, so I think I'll probably spend more time thinking about this.

Two more chapters to come!

Chapter 4: Shadow Stalker

Notes:

HQM and Derived's beta contributions were excellent, and tbh they basically wrote this fic on their own. By which I mean I'll be taking all the credit and none of the blame.

(See the end of the chapter for more notes.)

Chapter Text

Underground bases were supposed to be cool. Secret lairs, armed minions, and a host of traps and tricks. Getting in and out was supposed to be a challenge, a feat worthy of a film adaptation, or a limited comic book run. Instead, it was pitifully easy. Half the base was unpowered, and the other half was easy enough to disable with only one of Dragon's drones. After that, it was just a matter of getting in, shooting the snake in the back with a tranq dart, then creeping through the rest of the base to knock out the rest of the guards. A feat made simpler by other heroes attacking though each entrance the moment the power was cut.

"Left," says the obnoxious voice in her ear. The tinker tech earpiece doesn’t interfere with Shadow Stalker’s breaker state, which she’s found to be both a blessing and a curse. All the benefit gained through extra intel is outweighed by who’s giving it to her.

Shadow Stalker goes left, and shoots a dart into another mercenary. "You sure know an awful lot about this place," she says under hear breath.

"Told you, I used to work for this guy. Another pair on your right."

Two darts is all she needs to dispatch them. "Used to. Sure."

"You still think this is a trap?" Tattletale sounds more amused than offended.

"You have a lot of grudges against me," Shadow Stalker points out.

"True, but if It wanted my revenge I'd have it. Besides, I promised I would leave you alone." Something in her tone catches Shadow Stalker's attention. Softness?

"Who made you promise that?"

Any response Tattletale might have given is interrupted by Miss Militia. "Less chatter, girls. Stalker, how many left?"

Tattletale responds for her. "Four, including Coil."

"I already got Coil," Shadow Stalker snaps.

"You got his body double," Tattletale corrects.

"You told me I was going for the real one." Shadow Stalker grits her teeth, and shoots another guard.

"Because you were. Problem is, you were always going to get the double first. Unless we got lucky. I'd explain it, but it's kinda complicated and you probably wouldn't get it."

This was beginning to piss her off. "What, like that quantum thingie? With the cat? Where you can't tell which it is until you interact with it? What was that name… something German…"

"Huh. Yeah, that’s about right.” The shock in Tattletale’s voice makes this entire mess worth it.

"Schrödinger's cat," Shadow Stalker says triumphantly. She turns a corner and changes to mist just in time to avoid a pair of laser blasts.

"Shadow Stalker, of course," comes a smooth voice from down the hall.

Two guards flank a man wearing a black bodysuit with a white snake coiled over it. In front of him is a young girl, and in his hand is a gun, held at her head.

"Shit." Shadow Stalker rematerializes just in time to hear Tattletale's curse. "I was hoping she'd still be out of commission."

"Who?" Shadow Stalker demands.

It's Miss Militia who answers. "Dinah Alcott, a parahuman who can predict the future."

‘Shit’ is right.

"Stall," Tattletale orders.

For once, Shadow Stalker doesn't protest. "Hiding behind a kid, huh?"

She swears Coil is smiling at her. "The threat isn't empty, I assure you."

Shadow Stalker tenses up; she believes him. This was the guy Tattletale worked for? Explains why she was so quick to jump ship.

Her headpiece crackles, and the two mercenaries tighten their grip.

"Stalker." Miss Militia again. "Listen to me carefully. When Tattletale says jump, go for the kid. Ignore everything else, prioritize her."

Shadow Stalker flicks her gaze across her opponents. She could probably take them. One mercenary would go down immediately. The other she could dodge. Coil would be a problem, but if he tried to attack her he'd leave the kid open to escape. Although, her glassy eyes makes it seem unlikely that she'd try.

Does Shadow Stalker really trust Tattletale? No, not really. Miss Militia? Hardly. She doesn't trust most people, and that tended to work out for her. Instinct hadn't failed her so far, so she would trust that. She'd trust herself.

"Jump."

Shadow Stalker leaps forward, diving between two lasers without shifting to her shadow state. Half a second later, a bullet passes through where her head would be if she didn't turn to mist that same second. Then she's back in physical form, and firing two tranq darts at the mercenaries. Both miss, but there’s a flash of light they go down anyway. Rather than look for the source of her assistance, she grabs the kid and rolls around Coil's body. There's a sharp bang, and followed by a heavy thump. A glance confirms that Coil is down, and another confirms the source.

Standing at the end of the hall, behind where Coil stood, is Miss Militia, holding a smoking gun. On the other end of the hallway, back from where Shadow Stalker had approached, is Lady Photon, who likely took down the guards.

"Nice," Tattletale's voice crackles through the headset. "Sound off?"

"Uber and Leet are down," come's Brandish's voice through the headset. "Circus was there too, but she slipped away."

"Trainwreck surrendered," Assault says next. "Might be amenable to a deal."

"Coil is down," Miss Militia says crisply.

"Kid Win and I will start cracking his computers," Dragon supplies.

Shadow Stalker stands up, heart thudding in her chest. She didn't know most of this was happening. Segmented plans, or whatever. It makes sense, she has to admit, given the scale of this. Especially if Coil's powers made him that slippery.

"I got the Alcott girl," Shadow Stalker says. She didn't know this was her mission until now, but she's not about to let anyone else know that.

"And I've got a headache, so I'm gonna pop some pills until it's time for the briefing." Tattletale's faux cheer can't hide the exhausted relief in her voice.

Throughout the rest of the cleanup, Shadow Stalker floats numbly from place to place. The more she sees of this base, of this plan, and the more she learns of the circumstances surrounding this, the more surprised she becomes that things even worked out. Tattletale really helped set this up? Coil had this many minions? This much money and power?

What on earth would possess someone to betray someone like this?

 

Notes:

Wow I totally forgot to type a note before posting.

Sophia is one of my fav characters, and I wanted to let her be cool. It's a bit beyond what they'd normally have Wards do, but then this is exceptional circumstances and they had a narrow window where Coil wouldn't be ready for them. Breaking the truce? To save a preteen girl from a supervillain? I think the cape community will forgive this—

Final chapter tomorrow!

Chapter 5: Victoria Dallon

Notes:

Many thanks to HQM and Derived for the beta assistance.

(See the end of the chapter for more notes.)

Chapter Text

Victoria Dallon is conflicted. Tattletale, her nemesis and the worst person she knows, helped take down a major villain. Tattletale, who never takes anything seriously, was on her best behavior during the entire briefing, even shutting up when Director Piggot told her to. Most damning of all…

Tattletale, who needles and lies for fun, wasn't lying about Amy.

The hospital is loud, crowded, and a decidedly unpleasant place to be at the best of times. These are not the best of times, obviously, but Victoria almost welcomes the chaos. She and her sister just had a talk, and the implications are… well... Victoria didn't expect Amy to admit to having feelings for her. Nor the outpouring of bitter resentment and frustration that followed.

What had started as an attempt to help her sister, to offer comfort and love—familial love, obviously—turned into a cocktail of bitter emotions that she wasn’t ready to swallow. How is she meant to process this? Especially now, with how much she’s already lost.

Walking around the hospital helps, but her mind keeps going back to that argument. To Amy storming out. To the last conversation Victoria had with her mom, where both of them ended up shouting. To Tattletale, who never seems to actually cross the line when needling her, despite how often it feels like she should have. The contrast is nearly as upsetting as the last day has been.

Maybe that's giving the villain too much credit. Maybe—something in her peripheral vision catches her attention. Victoria jerks to a stop, and doubles back to find a very familiar girl sitting beside a hospital bed; Tattletale, out of costume, next to a dark haired girl on life support. Victoria is familiar enough with hospitals by now to recognize a long term care situation, and unfortunately very familiar with the specific setup for people in comas.

Her dad has a setup very similar to this, after all.

Victoria stands at the door, torn between calling out or walking away. Pretending she didn't see anything is still an option, right?

Tattletale looks at one of the monitors, and sighs. "Might as well come in, Glory Girl."

Victoria steps into the room, and notices the reflection in the glare on the screen. "Didn't expect to see you here, Tats."

The ex-villain winces. "Just call me Lisa. It's easier that way."

Lisa. A name to go with the face. "Nice to meet you, Lisa."

Victoria hovers awkwardly by the bed, and looks over the girl laying in it. She's a bit younger than Lisa, by Victoria's reckoning. Dark hair, recently cut to shoulder length. A flat face, with a thin wide mouth. A pair of glasses sits optimistically by her beside table, alongside what appears to be an ant farm.

"Say hello to Skitter, Victoria," Lisa says softly. "Last remaining member of the Undersiders."

Victoria doesn't speak. What is she supposed to say to that?

"Even that title stops being accurate when she wakes up," Lisa continues sadly. "She wanted to be a hero, you know. Joined up with us instead, but never really gave up on it. She won't admit it, but part of that was because she was lonely, and scared that the Wards wouldn't like her."

Lisa chuckles. It's a sad, hollow noise.

"That's part of why I'm doing this, you know. So that when she wakes up, she has a friend in the Wards to make the transition easier." Lisa reaches over, and grips her sleeping friend’s hand. “That, and the heroes were going to take her anyway. Coma fighting Leviathan? They’d have to give her proper care, but unless I came over too they wouldn’t keep her safe. Not for lack of trying, of course, but...”

Coil. Victoria only knows pieces of the story, but it’s enough to paint a bleak picture.

She swallows. It was obvious from the beginning that Tattletale was a mask of some sort. Victoria knew that intellectually, even if it didn’t matter until now. At some point, she stopped trying to look under it and gave up on ever seeing the girl on the other side. She thought they weren't that different, and the nuance was subtle enough as to not be worth dwelling on. Clearly, Victoria was wrong.

"Coil's gone. You don't know what that means for me. Nobody does. I can do anything I want, go anywhere, do anything. Instead, I'm staying here with people who hate me." Lisa looks at Victoria, and the mask is back up. "Why do you think that is, Glory Girl?"

"Because you're a good friend, Lisa." Victoria puts a hand on Lisa's shoulder, and squeezes gently. "You're a good person."

"I wouldn't go that far," Lisa says with a roll of her eyes. She turns back to look at Skitter, but doesn't shrug off Victoria's hand. "Sorry about your sister, by the way."

"You tried to help?" It comes out as a question.

"Sorta. Not that hard. I haven't decided if I regret that yet."

She's open right now. Vulnerable. Victoria could probably push harder. Get more out of her. Figure out what makes her tick.

Instead, she stays silent, and lets the clock tick further towards the end of visiting hours.

Lisa takes a shuddering breath, then relaxes. Another in, another out. She’s not crying, but she could be. All it would take is a nudge in the right direction.

"You know, if you wanted advice on a rebrand name, I'm sure I could come up with something less childish than Tattletale," Victoria says.

Lisa barks out a laugh. "Coming from person who picked Glory Girl? If I let you have any input, I'd get called something like Tongue Twister."

Victoria snorts. "I can just see the innuendo now. I was thinking of something more distinguished, actually. Maybe it could pay homage to your skill with words."

Lisa raises an eyebrow at Victoria.

"Something like, The Cunning Lin—"

"Don't you dare finish that sentence, Glory Hole," Lisa snaps.

The banter undoes a knot that Victoria hadn't realized was there. Tension bleeds out of her, and her mood lightens. She'll still have to deal with her family, of course. Working things out with Amy is likely to be hard, and her mom still isn’t happy that Victoria wants to move out. All the same, it's what Victoria wants. What she needs.

In an odd way, she has Lisa to thank for this realization.

Now if only Victoria could figure out how to vocalize that.

 

Notes:

And here it is.

Several people in the comments have already guessed this outcome, which is kinda neat lol.
The fate of the other Undersiders is somewhat up in the air, but there were definitely deaths. I'm going to keep the details of that to myself, because I'm poking at a sequel and if that ever ends up written it would be more fun to reveal it then.

Part of this fic was a mental exercise I've been turning over in my head for a while now. "How do you get Lisa to willingly join the Wards post Leviathan?" And it kinda hit me all at once the other day, so here we are lol.

Victoria is a fun character, and one of the characters I'm somewhat stuck on right now. I've been having a lot of fun writing her and Lisa lately, and this was no exception.
With canon happening more or less the same, aside from the leviathan fight itself, addressing Amy is an inevitability. Lisa picked up where Dean left off, sort of, in the sense that she wanted to "defuse" the Amy bomb. Unfortunately, Lisa is starting from a worse place than Dean was, and Amy is predisposed against her. Additionally, Lisa is less concerned with Amy's wellbeing than with Victoria's, and her approach reflects that. Still, this has the effect of making it go off in a slightly more stable way. For now, anyway.

Overall I had a lot of fun writing this, and I hope everyone enjoyed. The response has been heartening, so thank you.
